 Preview: Utah Jazz End Road Trip With Matchup Against Timberwolves 
 Eric Spyropoulos ● @EricSpyroNBA Digital Writer November 7, 2026 4:25 PM MST The Utah Jazz are looking to snap out of an early-season funk. 
 Utah has had to deal with adversity in several forms, from injuries to the team’s frontcourt rotation to cold shooting, which has resulted in a seven-game losing streak. The Jazz are coming off an NBA Cup loss to the Dallas Mavericks on Friday night, a game in which they knocked down threes (15 of them), but were outmatched in the possession game as a result of 21 turnovers and the 21 offensive rebounds that Dallas grabbed.
 Lauri Markkanen (24 points, eight made threes) and Darryn Peterson (21 points, five assists) helped Utah’s offense during different stages of the game, but the Mavericks got significant production off the bench (44 points, including a 13-point, 17-rebound double-double from rookie Morez Johnson Jr.) and got to the free-throw line (25-of-31) to pull away for the 112-100 victory.
 The fourth and final stop on Utah’s road trip brings them to Minneapolis for a first meeting of the season against the Minnesota Timberwolves.
 Although Minnesota (7-3) has had to deal with the absence of Anthony Edwards, others have stepped up in his absence to continue pushing the Timberwolves forward. Chris Finch’s squad has won three in a row and entered Saturday with the league’s second-best net rating (plus-11.3 points per 100 possessions). 
 With the offseason acquisition of LaMelo Ball, Minnesota has an elite driver of the offense, while Ayo Dosunmu (17.3 points per game) and Jaden McDaniels (17.1 points per game) have stepped into larger roles on the offensive end. Of course, Rudy Gobert continues to anchor an elite defense, as the Timberwolves rank second in defensive rating.
 Minnesota won three of the four meetings between the two teams last season.
 Jazz injury report: 
 OUT - Trey Alexander (G League - Two-Way), Harrison Ingram (G League - Two-Way), Jaren Jackson Jr. (Right Knee; MCL Tear), Jusuf Nurkić (Right Foot; 2nd Plantar Plate Tear)
 QUESTIONABLE - Lauri Markkanen (Right Wrist; Sprain)
 Timberwolves injury report: 
 OUT - Donte DiVincenzo (Right Achilles Tendon; Repair/Surgery), Anthony Edwards (Right Knee; Arthroscopy)
 QUESTIONABLE - Joan Beringer (Nasal Fracture/Face Mask) 
 Here are three keys to Sunday’s game. 
 Protecting the defensive glass 
 The Timberwolves thrive in many areas, but one standout strength that should be a concern for Utah after Friday’s loss to Dallas is the offensive rebounding that Minnesota has generated. 
 The Timberwolves rank second in the league in offensive rebound percentage (35.6 percent), which has boosted an offense that has already been efficient from the field. Gobert (4.1 offensive rebounds per game) and second-year big man Joan Beringer (3.3 per game) have been the main drivers of this success on the glass and will test Utah’s shorthanded frontcourt.
 After Friday’s game against the Mavericks, the Jazz slipped to 10th in defensive rebound percentage, an area of their defense that had been a strength to begin the season. Utah will need all five players on the floor to box out and collapse towards the rim in hopes of limiting Minnesota to one shot on each trip down the floor.
 Limiting turnovers  
 Utah’s struggles in the possession game on Friday were twofold. 
 Not only did Dallas grab 21 offensive rebounds, but the Jazz turned it over 21 times on the offensive end, which prevented them from maintaining a flow and helped the Mavericks generate an advantage in shot attempts.
 Sunday’s matchup against Minnesota’s defense will once again test Utah’s ball security. The Timberwolves rank eighth in opponent turnover percentage, with long and physical defenders scattered throughout Finch’s rotation that are able to wreck havoc on opposing offenses. 
 Utah entered Saturday ranked 25th in turnover percentage (17.6 percent), a number that will have to be lowered in hopes of pulling off an upset win Sunday night. 
 The continued search for consistent offense  
 In the beginning of Friday’s game against Dallas, it appeared that the Jazz were going to rely on effective ball movement and timely shot-making to break out of an offensive slump.
 Despite 11 turnovers in the first half, Utah had scored 57 points, had dished out 17 assists, and knocked down seven 3-pointers. The ball was moving, with it often finding Markkanen beyond the arc as the visitors kept pace with Dallas.
 Unfortunately, the turnover issues maintained in the second half while the ball movement stagnated. The Jazz ended the night with 25 assists and those aforementioned 21 turnovers. 
 “In the first half, we really moved the ball and had a great flow to us,” Jazz head coach Will Hardy said postgame. “But in the second half, we didn’t have the same tempo.”
 Peterson found a groove in the fourth quarter (12 points), Markkanen has been lighting it up from deep in recent games (17 made threes over the last three contests), and Keyonte George just had a 39-point outburst a few days ago. However, the search remains for a consistent 48 minutes on that end of the floor, which will be a necessity Sunday in order to halt Minnesota’s momentum.
 Sunday’s game tips off at 5 p.m. MT. Tune in to the pregame show with Alema Harrington and Mike Smith beginning at 4:30 p.m. MT on Jazz+!
